deadline.value: For full consideration for departmental funding, completed fall applications must be received by December 1 of the preceding year.
deadline.quote: completed applications for Fall enrollment into Mason-Bioengineering PhD program must be received by December 1 of the preceding year

fee_waiver.value: Fall 2027 applicants who complete the application by November 15, 2026 get the application fee waived; this is not limited to domestic applicants.
fee_waiver.quote: We will waive the application fee for Fall 2027 applicants who have completed their application by November 15, 2026

gre_general.value: The catalog and department page do not mention the GRE.

gre_subject.value: Engineering has no GRE subject test.

supervisor.value: The application asks applicants to name two faculty they want to work with.
supervisor.quote: two faculty with whom they want to work

funding.value: The department page describes fellowships and funding timing but not how many students are funded.

entry_route.value: A bachelor's degree is required; up to 30 credits from a related master's can count.
entry_route.quote: Students must complete a minimum of 72 graduate credits, which may be reduced by a maximum of 30 credits from a related master's degree

toefl_min.value: College of Engineering and Computing programs accept TOEFL 4.5 (new scale) with no section minimum, or 80 for tests taken before January 21, 2026.
toefl_min.quote: College of Engineering and Computing graduate and undergraduate applicant score requirement: IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL 4.5 (80 if test is before January 21, 2026)

ielts_min.value: College of Engineering and Computing programs accept an IELTS overall band of 6.5 with no section minimum.
ielts_min.quote: College of Engineering and Computing graduate and undergraduate applicant score requirement: IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL 4.5 (80 if test is before January 21, 2026)

notes: Applicants are interviewed by a faculty committee, and those who skip the interview are disqualified. Fall 2027 fee waiver ends November 15, 2026.
